S074-01.notes: Two independent clauses ('Roosevelt resigned from the organization' / 'Anderson instead sang...') need comma + coordinating conjunction. A is a comma splice; B 'organization and, Anderson' misplaces the comma; D 'organization; and, Anderson' puts a semicolon before a conjunction and a stray comma after it.

S074-02.notes: The subject is the plural 'recordings', which is separated from the verb by an appositive phrase, so the verb must be 'are'. B 'is' and C 'has been' are singular. D 'being' leaves the sentence with no finite verb.

S074-03.notes: 'Among the best-selling recording artists' needs a plain plural; nothing is possessed. A and B are possessives with nothing following them to possess. C is singular, which doesn't work after 'among'.

S074-04.notes: The opening modifier 'Recovered and studied over the following years' must attach to the bones. In A it attaches to researchers, in C to a relative, and in D to Homo naledi, so all three are dangling modifiers.

S074-05.notes: After a complete clause, a colon correctly introduces the noun phrase that explains it: 'a frozen mixture... called pykrete'. B puts a semicolon before a fragment. C 'material that a frozen mixture...' and D 'material, which a frozen mixture...' each open a relative clause that never gets a verb.

S074-06.notes: The compound subject 'rim and ... walls' is plural, and the passage is in the present tense, so 'prevent' is correct. A and B are singular (and B's tense shift is also off). D 'preventing' is not a finite verb.

S074-07.notes: 'Fungi, whose glow results from...' is the possessive relative pronoun the sentence needs. A 'who's' means 'who is'. B 'which glow results' is ungrammatical. C 'their' turns the sentence into a comma splice.

flags.note: Option D duplicates the word after the blank: inserting it gives 'infrasound. Low-pitched low-pitched rumbles...'. D is wrong anyway (it creates a fragment), but the repetition is a construction defect and should be removed, e.g., make D 'infrasound. These'. Also, because the passage has a space after the blank, B renders as 'infrasound— low-pitched' with a space after the em dash; check how the dash will be typeset.

S074-08.notes: The dash correctly introduces the explanatory noun phrase. A puts a semicolon before a fragment. C is a comma splice and also creates 'it is ... rumbles'. D leaves a fragment after the period, and its repeated 'low-pitched' is the defect flagged above.

S074-09.notes: The subject is the singular 'Evidence'; the intervening phrase 'including ... iridium' is a trap. A and B are plural. D 'suggesting' is not a finite verb.

S074-10.notes: About 3,000 galaxies in a patch that looked empty means it was 'teeming'. B 'sparse' is the opposite. C 'unconnected' is unsupported. D 'obscured' doesn't fit the contrast with 'seemingly blank'.

S074-11.notes: 'Anxious buyers' purchasing 'comet pills' points to 'alarm'. A 'indifference' and B 'amusement' contradict that anxiety. C 'skepticism' is the reaction scientists wanted, not the one the reports caused.

S074-12.notes: The text sets up a gap (little was known about the surrounding city), then shows lidar filling it. A: the passage says nothing about construction dates. C: there is no comparison of building methods. D covers only one detail of the text.

S074-13.notes: Foote reported her results in 1856, before Tyndall began in 1859, which undercuts the claim that Tyndall was 'first'. A: no text questions Tyndall's accuracy. B: Foote's experiments involved carbon dioxide, not water vapor. D: Henry only read her paper aloud.

S074-14.notes: The text runs chronologically through the building's uses: cathedral, mosque, museum, mosque. B: the dome is never mentioned. C: the text makes no argument. D: no other buildings are compared.

S074-15.notes: The text contrasts hundreds of signs that took years to learn with 22 letters that spread widely, so a small set of letters made writing easier to learn and spread. A contradicts the order of events. B contradicts 'adapted'. C is an unsupported 'only' claim.

S074-16.notes: I checked the numbers: dart longest 9.0 > glider longest 8.9; glider average 8.4 > dart average 6.1. B covers both parts of the claim. A compares the glider with the stunt plane, not the dart. C covers only the first part. D is about longest throws, not averages.

S074-17.notes: If removing the surface particles restores the white color, the discoloration is on the surface and not a change in the stone. B is indirect: visitor numbers are not evidence about particles on the marble. C is irrelevant. D is consistent with several causes and doesn't single out pollution.

S074-18.notes: She saw the change coming and acted on it by learning FORTRAN, so 'Accordingly' fits. A: there is no contrast. B: there is no parallel case. D: learning FORTRAN is not an example of seeing the change coming.

S074-19.notes: Her petition responds to the barrier of a whites-only school, so 'In response' fits. A: there is no parallel. B: it is not an example. C: it is not a restatement.

flags.note: In B the appositive 'the system many people use daily on their phones' comes after 'calculations GPS needs', so it sits next to 'needs'/'calculations' rather than 'GPS'. The meaning is clear, but the wording is slightly awkward; 'supports the calculations needed by GPS, the system many people use...' would read better.

S074-20.notes: Only B connects West's model to GPS and daily phone use. A covers only the award, C only her start date, and D only GPS use with no mention of West.

S074-21.notes: The antecedent of 'which' is the plural 'bacteria' ('light' can't live in colonies), so 'live' is correct. A and B are singular and would match only 'light', which makes no sense. D 'living' leaves the relative clause with no finite verb.

S074-22.notes: Signed pots sold for more, and she also signed pots made by others. This suggests her signature itself, not who made the pot, raised its value. B assigns a motive the text doesn't support (she may have been helping the other potters sell). C is unsupported, since the price difference shows collectors did tell signed from unsigned. D is unsupported.
